topics.label: Introduction and Framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic, context, and challenges associated with studying the complement system.

topics.label: Foundations and Organization of the Complement System
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the structural organization, naming conventions, and central importance of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three upstream pathways through which complement recognizes targets and converges to activate C3.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream processes through which activated complement mediates pathogen elimination and inflammatory responses.

topics.label: Regulation and Host Cell Protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the molecular controls that prevent complement activation and damage on host cell surfaces.

topics.label: Clinical Pathologies of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how deficiencies in individual complement components produce distinct clinical diseases and vulnerabilities.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion Mechanisms and Biotechnology Applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how pathogens evade complement attack and how these bacterial evasion proteins are utilized in laboratory and medical applications.

topics.label: Conclusion and Looking Ahead
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the complement lecture and previews the next lecture on the adaptive immune system.
